topics.title: 20.1.1 Separating Acquisition, Processing, and Output
topics.summary: The engineering question in Separating Acquisition, Processing, and Output is not merely whether a program can be made to run. At this level, the useful question is what contract the mechanism establishes, which costs it moves elsewhere, and what evidence would distinguish a correct implementation from one that only succeeds on a convenient input. Streaming systems require explicit queue capacity and overload behavior. A production design therefore begins by naming the data, ownership, timing, and failure boundaries before choosing an optimization.

reading.title: 20.1.1 Separating Acquisition, Processing, and Output
paragraphs: The engineering question in Separating Acquisition, Processing, and Output is not merely whether a program can be made to run. At this level, the useful question is what contract the mechanism establishes, which costs it moves elsewhere, and what evidence would distinguish a correct implementation from one that only succeeds on a convenient input. Streaming systems require explicit queue capacity and overload behavior. A production design therefore begins by naming the data, ownership, timing, and failure boundaries before choosing an optimization.

For implementation work, separate correctness from performance. First construct a reference path whose behavior is easy to inspect, then introduce the parallel or hardware-specific path behind a narrow interface. Record dimensions, units, allocation ownership, synchronization points, and error returns. This makes the optimized path replaceable and gives tests something stronger than elapsed time to compare. When the implementation depends on CUDA, the CPU reference remains useful even on a machine without a GPU because it defines expected semantics independently of device execution.

Measurement must also match the claim. A kernel duration does not establish end-to-end latency; throughput does not establish deadline behavior; occupancy does not establish useful work; and a numerically close answer is not automatically acceptable unless the tolerance follows from the algorithm and application. Warm-up effects, transfer costs, synchronization, clock behavior, compiler options, device model, and input shape belong in the experiment record. Repeated measurements should be summarized rather than reduced to one unusually favorable observation.

A common failure pattern is to optimize the visible inner loop while leaving the dominant boundary unchanged. Examples include accelerating arithmetic while repeatedly transferring the same data, increasing concurrency while saturating memory bandwidth, or removing a lock while introducing unbounded queues. The corrective method is consistent: trace the complete request or sample path, locate the actual limiting resource, change one mechanism at a time, and rerun both correctness and performance checks.

Verification checkpoint. State the invariant that must remain true, the metric that matters, the environment in which it was measured, and the rollback or fallback path. If any of those four items is missing, the result is still an experiment rather than production evidence.

The corrective method is consistent: trace the complete request or sample path, locate the actual limiting resource, change one mechanism at a time, and rerun both correctness and performance checks.

Verification checkpoint. State the invariant that must remain true, the metric that matters, the environment in which it was measured, and the rollback or fallback path. If any of those four items is missing, the result is still an experiment rather than production evidence.

topics.summary: A high-performance subsystem should be specified with two parallel contracts: a semantic contract describing what result is correct and an operational contract describing the conditions under which that result must be delivered. blocks.text: The data path should be drawn before it is optimized. For a heterogeneous pipeline, identify where bytes originate, which component owns each buffer, when ownership or visibility changes, and where synchronization is required. A useful trace might be acquisition → host staging → transfer → device computation → result transfer → CPU decision → output. Every arrow has a cost and a failure mode. If a buffer is reused before an asynchronous consumer is finished, the bug is a lifetime violation even when the symptom appears as numerical noise.

blocks.text: Capacity planning follows from rates rather than intuition. If an input stage produces work faster than the slowest sustained downstream stage consumes it, a finite queue eventually fills. A larger queue postpones the failure while increasing worst-case latency. Production designs therefore define an overload policy: reject, drop according to an explicit rule, reduce fidelity, spill to a bounded secondary store, or apply backpressure upstream. The correct policy depends on the application, but “allocate until memory runs out” is not a policy.

blocks.text: Numerical verification deserves the same discipline. Floating-point operations may be associated differently on CPU and GPU, and parallel reductions can produce small differences without either implementation being conceptually wrong. The acceptance test should derive tolerances from the numerical problem and expected dynamic range. Use absolute tolerance near zero and relative or mixed tolerances where scale varies. For signal processing, also verify conventions such as FFT normalization, complex sign, bin mapping, windowing, and treatment of partial frames.

blocks.text: Performance experiments should separate latency, throughput, and utilization. Latency measures time for one unit of work through a defined boundary. Throughput measures completed work per unit time under a defined load. Utilization describes how busy a resource appears and is not itself a service outcome. A device can be highly utilized while useful throughput falls because of contention, retries, or inefficient memory access. Conversely, a low-utilization system may be correct when the workload is intentionally bursty.

blocks.text: For CUDA experiments, time the scope you intend to claim. Device events can measure intervals in a stream, while host clocks can measure end-to-end behavior including API and transfer costs. Asynchronous launches require an appropriate completion point before a host-side interval can be interpreted as completed GPU work. Record whether transfers use pageable or pinned memory, whether buffers are reused, and whether the first iteration includes context creation or one-time library initialization.

blocks.text: Resource cleanup must work on failure paths. Device allocations, streams, events, library handles, pinned host buffers, files, and threads all need owners. Wrap resources so destruction releases them and make move operations transfer ownership explicitly. Avoid a cleanup design that assumes every preceding initialization step succeeded. In a long-running service, a small leak per request is eventually a capacity incident.

blocks.text: Observability should answer questions without requiring a debugger on the production machine. Record configuration identity, input shape, queue depth, completed-work counters, bounded latency summaries, error counts, and hardware identity. A number named latency without milliseconds, microseconds, or a defined percentile is not operational evidence.

topics.title: Advanced review — from experiment to production evidence
topics.summary: A production review should reconstruct the causal chain from requirement to measurement. Begin with the workload: element count, sample rate, batch shape, arrival pattern, and numerical range. Then identify the implementation configuration: thread geometry, stream count, buffer sizes, algorithm/library selection, and CPU/GPU partition. Finally record the outcome with units. This structure makes a result comparable later; without it, “the optimized version was faster” cannot be reproduced or challenged.

blocks.text: Treat averages cautiously. A real-time or interactive system can satisfy an average while violating important tail deadlines. Preserve distributions or at least representative percentiles and maximum observations over a justified interval. Investigate outliers instead of deleting them because they make a graph untidy. They may expose allocation, page faults, synchronization, thermal behavior, scheduling interference, or periodic maintenance work.

blocks.text: Concurrency also changes the meaning of failure. An error observed by one stream or worker may occur after the initiating caller has continued. Define how failures propagate, whether new work is accepted after a fault, and how in-flight work is drained or cancelled. Shutdown deserves a test of its own: stop accepting work, signal producers and consumers, establish completion, release resources in dependency order, and verify that no background execution refers to destroyed state.

An optimization that leaks every device detail through the application can increase long-term maintenance cost even when its benchmark improves.

Callers should not need to know internal block sizes, scratch-buffer layout, or profiling instrumentation unless those details are genuine configuration contracts. This permits tuning without forcing application changes and makes CPU reference implementations easier to substitute in tests. An optimization that leaks every device detail through the application can increase long-term maintenance cost even when its benchmark improves.

Finally, document negative evidence. If multi-GPU execution, a particular compute capability, hard-real-time scheduling, or a vendor library path was not tested, say so. Engineering confidence comes from matching claims to evidence, not from making the evidence sound broader than it is. The result of this chapter should therefore be both an implementation and an evidence package: source revision, configuration, tests, measurements, limitations, and the decision they support.
